nodes.goal: Give every building a height in metres for Rasterize Buildings: Overture's height, else its number of floors times the floor height, else the default height; leave out underground buildings and keep id, height, num_floors, class and the footprint.
nodes.title: Building heights
nodes.content:
# Rasterize Buildings reads a "height" column in metres with a value in every
# row. Overture gives most buildings a height; for the rest, take the number of
# floors times the floor height, and else the default height.
buildings = input_0[~input_0["is_underground"].fillna(False).astype(bool)]
height = buildings["height"].fillna(buildings["num_floors"] * float([!! floor_height !!]))
buildings = buildings.assign(height=height.fillna(float([!! default_height !!])))
# Overture's nested columns (names, sources) are not needed downstream.
buildings = buildings[["id", "height", "num_floors", "class", "geometry"]].reset_index(drop=True)
# Mark the frame as buildings, so an Autark map extrudes each footprint to its height.
buildings.metadata = {"layerType": "buildings"}
return buildings

nodes.goal: Keep the named parks (input_0) of at least the minimum area that are not mostly under the building footprints (input_1), a park mapped twice once; one row per park with its name as park, osm_id, area_m2 and outline, in EPSG:4326.
nodes.title: Open-air parks
nodes.content:
# The named parks large enough to measure, in the open: a "park" mostly under
# building footprints, such as a public atrium, is left out. Areas in metres,
# in the UTM zone of the parks, so this works for any city.
utm = input_0.estimate_utm_crs()
parks = input_0[input_0["name"].notna() & input_0.geometry.type.isin(["Polygon", "MultiPolygon"])]
parks = parks.to_crs(utm)
area = parks.area
roofed = parks.intersection(input_1.to_crs(utm).union_all()).area / area
parks = parks[(area >= float([!! min_area !!])) & (roofed < 0.5)].assign(area_m2=area)
# One park mapped twice (two outlines that almost coincide, under two names)
# counts once: the larger outline is kept.
kept = []
for i in parks.sort_values("area_m2", ascending=False).index:
    if not any(parks.geometry[i].intersection(parks.geometry[k]).area >= 0.8 * parks.area_m2[i]
               and parks.area_m2[k] <= 1.25 * parks.area_m2[i] for k in kept):
        kept.append(i)
parks = parks.loc[sorted(kept)]
parks = parks.rename(columns={"name": "park"})[["park", "osm_id", "area_m2", "geometry"]]
# A park's name is its key in the charts: two parks with one name keep their OSM id.
twice = parks["park"].duplicated(keep=False)
parks.loc[twice, "park"] = parks["park"] + " (" + parks["osm_id"].astype(str) + ")"
return parks.to_crs(4326).sort_values("park").reset_index(drop=True)

nodes.goal: Mark the buildings (input_0) the what-ifs change, by one rule for every park (input_1): around_park when at least the Tall building height tall and within the Distance from a park of any park, in metres in the parks' UTM zone; with each building's nearest_park and park_distance_m.
nodes.title: Buildings around parks
nodes.content:
import pandas as pd

# The buildings the what-ifs change, by one rule for every park, so the parks
# compare fairly: at least the Tall building height tall, and within the
# Distance from a park of any park. input_0 is the buildings, input_1 the parks.
# Distances in metres, in the parks' UTM zone.
buildings, parks = input_0, input_1
utm = parks.estimate_utm_crs()
footprints = buildings.to_crs(utm).geometry
distance = pd.DataFrame({park: footprints.distance(outline)
                         for park, outline in zip(parks["park"], parks.to_crs(utm).geometry)})
marked = buildings.assign(nearest_park=distance.idxmin(axis=1), park_distance_m=distance.min(axis=1))
marked["around_park"] = ((marked["height"] >= float([!! @tall_height !!]))
                         & (marked["park_distance_m"] <= float([!! @park_distance !!])))
# assign drops the frame's metadata: mark it as buildings again.
marked.metadata = {"layerType": "buildings"}
return marked

nodes.goal: Take out the buildings Buildings around parks marks.
nodes.title: Data Transformation - Towers removed
nodes.content:
# Towers removed: the buildings Buildings around parks marks are taken out.
remaining = input_0[~input_0["around_park"]].reset_index(drop=True)
# SCOUT's rasterizer looks rows up by position, hence reset_index; filtering
# drops the frame's metadata, so mark it as buildings again.
remaining.metadata = {"layerType": "buildings"}
return remaining

nodes.goal: Cut the buildings Buildings around parks marks down to the Tall building height.
nodes.title: Data Transformation - Height cap
nodes.content:
# Height cap: the buildings Buildings around parks marks are cut down to the
# Tall building height; every other building keeps its height.
cap = float([!! @tall_height !!])
capped = input_0.assign(height=input_0["height"].where(~input_0["around_park"], cap))
capped.metadata = {"layerType": "buildings"}
return capped

nodes.goal: Rasterize the existing buildings into zoom-16 height tiles.
nodes.title: Rasterize Buildings - Existing
nodes.content:
"""Rasterize Buildings: SCOUT's building rasterizer, "OSM vector to raster".

Input: a buildings layer, a GeoDataFrame of polygons with a CRS and a column
of heights in metres.
Output: the 256 by 256 tiles SCOUT writes, 8-bit gray where 255 is the maximum
height, in EPSG:3395, saved as one of this dataflow's computed datasets, under
the name the "Save tiles as" widget gives ("tiles"); and a table of them, one
row per tile: zoom, x, y and the maximum height. Mosaic Tiles, given the same
name, puts the tiles together into one raster.
The Widgets tab sets the height column, the zoom level, the maximum height and
the name.
Ported from SCOUT, https://github.com/urban-toolkit/scout.
"""
from scout_raster_conversion.convert_to_raster import convert_raster
from scout_raster_conversion.mosaic import tile_table

tiles = curio_save_folder([!! tiles !!])
convert_raster(input_0, [!! attribute !!], int([!! zoom !!]), tiles, max_height=float([!! max_height !!]))
return tile_table(tiles, int([!! zoom !!]), float([!! max_height !!]))

nodes.goal: Predict the existing buildings' accumulated shadow with Deep Umbra.
nodes.title: Accumulated Shadow - Existing
nodes.content:
"""Accumulated Shadow: SCOUT's Deep Umbra shadow model.

Input: Rasterize Buildings' table of tiles (scout.raster-conversion). The
height tiles themselves are this dataflow's computed dataset the "Tiles"
widget names, the name Rasterize Buildings saved them under ("tiles").
Output: (shadow, metrics).
- shadow: the accumulated shadow in minutes, one raster in EPSG:3395 on the
  grid of the tiles' height mosaic (Mosaic Tiles), made from the shadow tiles
  SCOUT's run_shadow_model writes. An Autark map draws it, band band_1.
- metrics: SCOUT's metrics as its run_shadow_model computes them, one row:
  "Mean Acc shadow" and "Median Acc shadow", the minutes of shadow over the
  ground (the cells with no building), for a chart comparing the scenarios.
The shadow tiles are kept as a computed dataset of this dataflow, under the
name the "Save shadows as" widget gives.
The Widgets tab sets the season and the names. The model is the Model
Catalog's Deep Umbra, model.scout.deep-umbra, its ONNX file run as it is.
Ported from SCOUT, https://github.com/urban-toolkit/scout.
"""
from scout_shadow.deep_umbra import run_shadow_model
from scout_shadow.mosaic import mosaic

shadows = curio_save_folder([!! shadows !!])
metrics = run_shadow_model(
    curio_computed_path([!! tiles !!]),
    [!! @season !!],
    shadows,
    model_path=curio_load_model("model.scout.deep-umbra").entry,
)
return mosaic(shadows, [!! @season !!], curio_output_file), metrics

nodes.goal: Take the accumulated shadow raster from Accumulated Shadow.
nodes.title: Shadow raster - Existing
nodes.content:
# Accumulated Shadow returns (shadow, metrics): this is the shadow in minutes, a raster.
return input_0[0]

nodes.goal: For each park (input_1), the accumulated shadow raster's cells inside it (input_0, minutes, EPSG:3395): mean, median and 90th percentile minutes, the mean as a share of the season's daylight of the Season parameter (SCOUT's 720 minutes in summer, 540 in spring, 360 in winter), and the shares of its cells in sun (under 25% of daylight), partial shade and deep shade (over 75%). One row per park, with its outline and area.
nodes.title: Shade per park - Existing
nodes.content:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rasterio.features import geometry_mask

# input_0: the accumulated shadow in minutes, a raster; input_1: the parks.
shadow, parks = input_0, input_1
# The minutes of daylight Deep Umbra's season stands for, SCOUT's factor.
daylight = {"winter": 360, "spring": 540}.get([!! @season !!], 720)
minutes = shadow.read(1, masked=True).filled(np.nan).astype("float64")
rows = []
for park in parks.to_crs(shadow.crs).itertuples():
    inside = geometry_mask([park.geometry], out_shape=minutes.shape, transform=shadow.transform, invert=True)
    values = minutes[inside]
    values = values[~np.isnan(values)]
    if values.size == 0:
        continue
    share = values / daylight
    rows.append({
        "park": park.park,
        "cells": int(values.size),
        "mean_min": float(values.mean()),
        "median_min": float(np.median(values)),
        "p90_min": float(np.percentile(values, 90)),
        "pct_daylight": float(values.mean() / daylight),
        # Shares of the park's cells: in sun (shaded under a quarter of the
        # daylight), in partial shade, and in deep shade (over three quarters).
        "share_sun": float((share < 0.25).mean()),
        "share_partial": float(((share >= 0.25) & (share < 0.75)).mean()),
        "share_deep": float((share >= 0.75).mean()),
    })
return parks.merge(pd.DataFrame(rows), on="park")

# The minutes of shadow each park loses from Existing (input_0) to Towers
# removed (input_1) and to Height cap (input_2): the sun it gains under each,
# on its outline for the maps.
existing = input_0.set_index("park")["mean_min"]
gained = input_0[["park", "area_m2", "geometry"]].copy()
for column, what_if in (("gain_removed_min", input_1), ("gain_capped_min", input_2)):
    gained[column] = (existing - what_if.set_index("park")["mean_min"]).reindex(gained["park"]).values
return gained
